rows.jp: 相変わらず、睦美おばさんの姿はない。
rows.en: As usual, there's no sign of Aunt Mutsumi.

ghs.en: As it always is, Mutsumi-obasan is nowhere to be seen.

rows.jp: 当たり前である。
rows.en: Naturally.

ghs.en: That's obvious,

rows.jp: 死んだんだから。
rows.en: She's dead, after all.

ghs.en: because she has died.

rows.jp: いや、死んだのだろうか。
rows.en: Or is she?

ghs.en: No, wait, has she actually died?

rows.jp: 人類全員かくれんぼ説もまだ生きている。
rows.en: My theory that the entire human race is playing hide-and-seek is still alive.

ghs.en: The theory that the whole of mankind is playing hide-and-seek still survives.

rows.jp: 脳だいぶヒビ割れちゃってるんじゃない？と思わんばかりにくだらない説だが、比定する根拠はない。
rows.en: It's stupid enough to make you wonder whether my brain has cracked wide open, but I have no grounds for ruling it out.

ghs.en: "Didn't your brain split nice and clean now?", is how worthless that theory is if I think about it, but I have no grounds to make a competing hypothesis.

rows.jp: 産業もエネルギーも報道もうっちゃってかくれんぼとは、人類も弾けたものである。
rows.en: Humanity must really have gone off the deep end, ditching industry, energy, and the news for a game of hide-and-seek.

ghs.en: A game of hide-and-seek in which manufacture, energy production, and information services are abandoned means mankind's gotta have snapped as well.

rows.jp: 滅亡滅亡言っているが、実際は消失なわけで。
rows.en: I keep calling it extinction, but disappearance is all I actually know.

ghs.en: Fallen, it's fallen I can say all day, but fact is that it's just a case of disappearance.

rows.jp: さておき、優しい睦美おばさんが出てこないわけだ。
rows.en: Anyway, that explains why kind Aunt Mutsumi won't come out.

ghs.en: Regardless, gentle Mutsumi-obasan does not turn up.

rows.jp: 家にまったく家族臭が感じられない。
rows.en: There's no whiff of family left in the house.

ghs.en: Damn if I just can't feel that flavor of family in this house.

rows.jp: もともと希薄だったが、まったくなくなってしまった。
rows.en: There was never much to begin with. Now there's none.

ghs.en: It was thin and sparse from the start, but now it's all entirely damnably gone.

rows.jp: 洗い場をのぞく。
rows.en: I peer into the wash area.

ghs.en: I peek in the laundry room.

rows.jp: 水を張ったタライの中に、トマトがみっつ浮いていた。
rows.en: Three tomatoes float in a basin of water.

ghs.en: In a washtub filled to the brim with water, tomatoes, three, were floating.

rows.jp: 「トマトじゃ」
rows.en: “Behold—tomatoes.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Tomatoes, ain't they."

rows.jp: 驚いた。
rows.en: I'm amazed.

ghs.en: I was surprised.

rows.jp: 俺が入れたものではない。
rows.en: I hadn't put them there.

ghs.en: I didn't put them there.

rows.jp: さっそく食う。
rows.en: I eat one on the spot.

ghs.en: I promptly eat.

rows.jp: 新鮮なトマトだ。
rows.en: It's fresh.

ghs.en: They're fresh tomatoes.

rows.jp: 口の中で、詰まった実がじゅわっと潰れた。
rows.en: The firm flesh bursts in my mouth, flooding it with juice.

ghs.en: The dense fruit crushes juicily inside the mouth.

rows.jp: 頬がひきつるほどうまい。
rows.en: So good my cheeks twitch.

ghs.en: Delicious enough to want to suck on the cheeks.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the taste is so good that the speaker's cheeks twitch; the English instead describes wanting to suck on cheeks.

highlights.text: Delicious enough to want to suck on the cheeks.

rows.jp: とにかくこの家に食い物はないのだ。
rows.en: There is absolutely nothing to eat in this house.

ghs.en: Regardless, there's nothing to eat at home.

rows.jp: いつも睦美さんが会社帰りにできあいを買ってきてくれた。
rows.en: Mutsumi always picked up prepared food on her way home from work.

ghs.en: Mutsumi-san would always buy and bring something ready-made on the way back from the company.

rows.jp: だから料理の機会は少なく、材料も常備されていない。
rows.en: So we rarely had reason to cook, and never kept ingredients around.

ghs.en: With opportunities for cooking therefore rare, there is no reserve of ingredients.

rows.jp: そういやじゃがいもだけはあった気がする……。
rows.en: Come to think of it, I vaguely remember some potatoes...

ghs.en: But come to think of it, it feels as if there's potatoes...

rows.jp: 机の上を見ると、メモが置いてあった。
rows.en: There's a note on the table.

ghs.en: Looking on top of the table, there was a note set there.

rows.jp: 『夕食がないこともない』
rows.en: ‘It’s not like there won’t be dinner.’

ghs.en: 『There may be no absence of dinner.』

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんか。
rows.en: Youko?

ghs.en: Youko-chan then.

rows.jp: 食い物で釣ろうとしている。
rows.en: She's trying to lure me with food.

ghs.en: Trying to lure me in, using food as bait.

rows.jp: ありありと。
rows.en: And not subtly.

ghs.en: Veeery obviously too.

rows.jp: そんな手に俺が乗るか、冷静に考えればわかることだ。
rows.en: One calm moment's thought tells me whether I'd fall for a trick like that.

ghs.en: If I think calmly I will understand whether I should fall for that trick.

rows.jp: 「いってきます」
rows.en: “I'm off.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm going out!"

rows.jp: 行くに決まっていた。
rows.en: Of course I'm going.

ghs.en: I had decided to go.

rows.jp: 蝋燭に火を灯す。
rows.en: I light a candle.

ghs.en: I ignite the wick of a candle.

rows.jp: 日記を書く。
rows.en: I write in the diary.

ghs.en: I write the diary.

rows.jp: 克明に書く。
rows.en: I record every last detail.

ghs.en: I write thoroughly, diligently.

rows.jp: 来週のために―――
rows.en: For next week—

ghs.en: For the sake of next week---
